# Results (generated by scripts/make_results_doc.py from results/experiments/)

All numbers: mean over 5 held-out seeds (1001-1005); DRL rows are aggregated over 3 training seeds. Models were trained on the **steady** regime only, so diurnal/bursty are generalisation tests.


## Regime: bursty

| Policy | Hotspot freq. | Peak T (C) | IT energy | Completed | Dropped | Return |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random | 0.603 | 65.8 | 10523.1 | 903.4 | 544.4 | -3680.7 |
| round-robin | 0.509 | 66.5 | 10800.0 | 903.4 | 544.4 | -3425.4 |
| greedy-utilisation | 0.292 | 64.2 | 10832.6 | 901.4 | 546.6 | -2717.7 |
| greedy-coolest | 0.223 | 64.2 | 10769.2 | 903.2 | 544.6 | -2594.5 |
| PPO | 0.453 | 64.0 | 9542.2 | 853.1 | 595.1 | -3021.5 |
| DQN | 0.123 | 51.2 | 4578.9 | 408.5 | 1054.5 | -3312.4 |

Best non-learning policy on hotspot frequency: **greedy-coolest** (0.223).
* PPO: hotspot 0.453 vs 0.223; completed 853 vs 903; return -3022 vs -2595.
* DQN: hotspot 0.123 vs 0.223; completed 409 vs 903; return -3312 vs -2595.

Best non-learning policy on hotspot frequency: **greedy-coolest** (0.245).
* PPO: hotspot 0.472 vs 0.245; completed 840 vs 877; return -1838 vs -1299.

## Interpretation (read with the tables)

* **Neither DRL agent beats the best heuristic (greedy-coolest) on a fair basis.**
  PPO's hotspot rate is close to round-robin and its return is worse than both greedy heuristics.
* **DQN's low hotspot rate is not a win.** It completes far fewer tasks (it defers
  most of the work), so it avoids heat by not doing the work. Its episode return is
  also worse than greedy-coolest. Treat it as a degenerate/partial always-defer policy.
* Possible explanations (hypotheses, not tested here): limited training budget
  (300k steps); reward weights that make deferral attractive; sparse/delayed thermal
  credit assignment; no action masking during training; no hyper-parameter tuning;
  heuristics that read exact temperature are very strong in a deterministic-ish simulator.
* Training seeds vary noticeably (see summary_per_run.csv); conclusions rest on 3 seeds only.
